en.intro_paragraph: Carats is a full-stack JavaScript framework that provides a modern development experience without relying on React. It uses JJSX for building user interfaces and supports both server-side and client-side rendering.
en.error_desc: The page you requested does not exist, or it was moved to a different version.
en.error_hint: If you followed a link from these docs, the target page is probably missing from the current version directory.
en.getting_started_intro: Learn how to set up a Carats project and get a server-rendered application running.
en.requirements_content: Carats uses Bun for package management and for running the development server. Bun transpiles TSX on the fly, so there is no separate compile step while developing. Node.js 20+ also works for production builds, but Bun is the supported path.
en.quickstart_desc: The fastest way to start is the official project generator. It writes a complete, working Carats application with facets, culets, a shared layout, SASS design tokens and tests, so every feature described in these docs is already wired up and can be read as working code.
en.quickstart_run: Install dependencies and start the dev server
en.manual_setup_desc: If you prefer to start from an empty project, create the folder structure below and install the dependencies yourself.
en.folder_structure_desc: Create the following folders and files. The locations are fixed because the framework resolves them by convention.
en.install_deps_desc: Carats is split into small packages. The runtime dependencies below are the ones used by a full-stack application; the dev dependencies are needed for JJSX transpilation, SASS and type checking.
en.tsconfig_desc: Carats requires a tsconfig.json at the root of the project. The types, jsx, jsxFactory and jsxFragmentFactory options are what teach TypeScript about JJSX, and typeRoots is what makes the global DTO interfaces in src/dto resolvable.
en.vite_client_desc: The client build runs in middleware mode because the Express server owns the HTTP listener. appType: 'custom' disables Vite's own HTML fallback, since Carats renders the HTML template itself.
en.package_scripts_desc: These scripts are the supported entry points for developing, building and previewing a Carats application.
en.run_desc: bun run dev starts the app with the Bun inspector on port 6499. bun run build bundles the server and the client, and bun run preview serves the production build. bun run build:static prerenders the app to static HTML.
en.structure_desc: A typical Carats project has the following structure:
en.desc_app_entry_point: Main application entry point. Mounts the Carats middleware on Express and starts the HTTP server.
en.desc_client_template: HTML template rendered by the server. Must contain the <!--app-head--> and <div id="app"><!--app-html--></div> placeholders.
en.desc_client_entrypoint: Client entrypoint. Mounts the facets on the browser and starts client-side rendering.
en.desc_route_definitions: Route definitions, shared by the client and the server entrypoint.
en.desc_vite_env: Vite client type reference. Lives at src/vite-env.d.ts, not inside src/client.
en.desc_base_sass: Global stylesheet holding the design tokens and base resets.
en.desc_pages: Page components. Each subfolder exports a default component from index.tsx and may import its own SASS file.
en.desc_server_entrypoint: Server entrypoint for SSR. Exports defineServerEntry(facets) and seats culets.
en.desc_server_functions: Culets, the server-side data functions used by burnished components.
en.desc_dto: Global TypeScript interfaces. Included through typeRoots so culet<User>(...) resolves without an import.
en.desc_public: Static assets served from the site root.
en.next_steps_desc: Read Core Concepts to understand how JJSX, facets, culets and server props fit together, then look at the Components and Server-Side Rendering pages.
en.core_concepts_intro: Understanding the core concepts of Carats will help you build applications more effectively.
en.jjsx_desc: JJSX enables a pure HTML & JavaScript experience similar to PHP. It allows you to write JavaScript code inside TSX files similar to React, but without React hooks or React DOM. Because components are plain functions that return HTML, the same component renders identically on the server and in the browser.
en.facets_desc: Facets are the routing system in Carats. They are a single object that maps route patterns to page components, and the same object is used by both the client and the server, so a route can never drift between the two. Facets are defined in src/client/facets.cara.ts and may declare route parameters, suspense states and whether in-app routing is enabled.
en.facets_partial_note: defineFacets accepts a partial definition, so routes and suspense are both optional. The reference template only declares error and notFound; omit loading unless a page genuinely suspends.
en.culets_desc: Culets are server-side functions that provide data to components. They are defined in src/server/culets and seated in the server entrypoint. Components that need server-side data are burnished, which makes the framework fetch from their culet automatically. A culet is matched to a page by its route string, so the route of the culet and the route of the facet must be identical.
en.seating_culets_desc: A culet defined in its own file is created with culet(route, handler) and then registered with seat(). seat returns the culet unchanged, so seating it is a pure registration step. Do not register the same culet a second time with another culet() call.
en.server_props_desc: Server props are the values a culet returns. The framework resolves them during server-side rendering, serializes them into the page, and passes them to the burnished component as its first argument. The component never fetches anything itself.
en.server_props_auto_text: Server props arrive as the first argument of a burnished component:
en.rendering_desc: Every page is rendered on the server first. The HTML template is filled in, the page component runs, and the resulting markup is sent to the browser together with the resolved server props. In the browser the same facets are mounted and the app takes over. A component function therefore runs in both places, which is why side effects must be deferred to afterMount or beforeMount.
en.client_runtime_desc: @carats/csr mounts the facets, intercepts internal link clicks when in-app routing is enabled, and exposes the serialized server props. window.carats.ssp.for holds the route the current server props belong to, and window.carats.ssp.data holds the props themselves. Prefer reading them through the framework rather than parsing the HTML, and use goTo for programmatic navigation.
en.components_intro: Carats components are similar to React components but with some key differences in how they handle attributes and events.
en.component_structure_desc: Components are .tsx files that export a default function. They receive a single props object, may declare defaultProps, and render props.children where the children should appear. They can import any file Vite understands, which is how SASS is attached to a component.
en.component_props_desc: Props are passed to components as expected, and children are contained within the component tags. A burnished component receives its culet's return value as props instead.
en.component_default_props_desc: defaultProps fills in props that were not supplied. This is the usual way to make a page renderable during a test, where no server props are available.
en.component_head_desc: Components can provide dynamic head tags (title, meta) by assigning to this.head inside the component function. The tags are collected during server-side rendering and injected into the <!--app-head--> placeholder of the HTML template.
en.component_head_note: this only exists in a component declared with the function keyword. An arrow function has no own this, so it cannot assign this.head; use a function declaration, or drop the head tags and keep the component as an arrow function. A regular arrow component is typed as CaratsComponent when it is used directly in a route, and as CaratsComponentWithThis when the annotation is needed for a plain function expression.
en.component_attributes_desc: HTML attributes are preserved as-is and are treated as strings. Unlike React, you cannot pass a function to an event attribute such as onclick or onsubmit; use addEventListener inside an afterMount callback instead. This is the single most common difference when porting React code.
en.burnish_desc: Burnished components automatically fetch data from their culet. Wrap your component with the Burnish function from @carats/render to enable this feature. The wrapper matches the component's route to a culet of the same route, so both must be registered under an identical route string.
en.burnish_recast: The framework caches the most recent server props for a route. Pass { recast: true } to refetch on every render instead of reusing the cached value.
en.client_entrypoint_desc: The entrypoint mounts the facets in the browser and then starts client-side rendering. clientRender() is required whenever in-app routing is enabled, and it should be called after mount.
en.vite_config_desc: The client Vite config builds from src/client and emits to dist/client with a manifest, which lets the server reference the hashed entry file.
en.server_side_intro: Carats provides automatic server-side rendering (SSR) through its @carats/ssr package.
en.server_entrypoint_desc: The server entrypoint is defined in src/server/entrypoint.ts using defineServerEntry from @carats/ssr. It binds the shared facets, registers culets, and exposes the render and getServerProps functions used by the server plugin.
en.culets_server_desc: Culets are defined using the culet function from @carats/ssr. Define one only when a route actually needs a server-side prop, and only when the data can be retrieved by a single GET request. The handler receives the request, including the route parameters, cookies, headers, query and method.
en.culet_seat_desc: A culet created in its own file must be registered with the seat function in the server entrypoint. Seating does not wrap or re-create the culet; it returns the same function so it can be used inline.
en.express_integration_desc: Carats is integrated with Express through @carats/express. The exported carats function returns a Router that renders pages, resolves server props and serves the built client assets, so it is mounted with app.use. This package requires Express 5.
en.server_vite_config_desc: The server bundle is built from src/server/entrypoint.ts into dist/server. publicDir is disabled because static assets belong to the client build.
en.hooks_intro: Carats gives you state and a client-side lifecycle through the @carats/hooks package.
en.use_hook_desc: The use function provides state management. Unlike React hooks it is not reactive: setting a value does not re-render anything, so nothing on the page updates by itself. The other half of the pair is subscribe, which is how a change becomes visible. Read the value while rendering, write the DOM from a subscriber, and change the value from anywhere.
en.use_manual_dom_note: Because there is no re-render, read the value while rendering and write the DOM from a subscriber:
en.use_interface: The use function returns a State object with get, set and subscribe methods. set accepts either a new value or a factory that receives the current one.
en.set_returns_note: set returns the new value, so you can use the result straight away when you need the updated number immediately.
en.subscribe_note: subscribe returns an unsubscribe function. Call it from the clear callback of an afterMount or beforeMount hook, otherwise the subscriber stays registered after the page is replaced.
en.aftermount_desc: The afterMount callback runs only on the client side, after the load event has been dispatched. Use it to reach DOM elements that the same component created, such as a counter label or a button. It may return a clear callback, which runs before the next hydration pass.
en.beforemount_desc: The beforeMount callback runs immediately on the client side, without waiting for the load event. Use it for work that does not need the markup of the component itself, such as timers, key listeners or subscriptions. Like afterMount, it may return a clear callback.
en.choosing_mount_hook_note: Reach for afterMount when the work depends on the markup this component produced, because it runs after the load event and the document is then guaranteed to be complete. Reach for beforeMount when it does not, such as a timer or a key listener, so that the work starts sooner.
en.clear_hydrations_desc: Clears all registered hydration callbacks by running their clear callbacks. This is mainly useful in tests and when tearing down an app manually.
en.hooks_no_react_note: There is no useEffect and no dependency array in Carats. A hook body runs on the server and on the client, so anything that touches the DOM or the network has to live inside a hook callback.
en.styling_intro: Carats uses scoped SASS for styling, promoting semantic HTML with minimal CSS classes.
en.base_sass_desc: The base.sass file in src/client contains global design tokens and style resets. All other SASS files import it with @use and as * so the tokens are available without a namespace prefix.
en.design_tokens_desc: Define colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints and other design tokens at the top level of base.sass. Do not nest them.
en.semantic_html_desc: Prefer semantic HTML elements with minimal class usage. Let the component structure and the design tokens handle the styling, and nest selectors in SASS instead of adding utility classes to the markup.
en.best_practices_intro: Follow these best practices for maintainable styling:
en.best_practice1: Define tokens at the top level. Never nest design tokens inside mixins or functions.
en.best_practice2: Prefer semantic HTML. Let the structure define the styling instead of adding classes.
en.best_practice3: Import base.sass correctly. Always use @use 'relative/path/to/base.sass' as *.
en.best_practice4: Keep specificity low. Avoid deeply nested selectors.
en.best_practice5: Use variables for consistency. Never hardcode colors, spacing or sizes.
en.routing_intro: Routing in Carats is data, not a filesystem. Every route is declared in a single facets object that the client and the server share.
en.routes_desc: The routes map goes from a route pattern to a page component. The pattern is matched exactly, except for segments that start with a colon, which capture a parameter.
en.dynamic_params_desc: A :name segment becomes a prop on the page component, and it is also available as params.name inside a culet for the same route. The name must match on both sides.
en.route_matching_note: Route patterns are matched by @carats/url with matchRoute. There is no wildcard, no optional segment and no catch-all: an unmatched URL renders the notFound suspense component instead.
en.in_app_routing_desc: With inAppRouting enabled, the client intercepts clicks on internal anchors and swaps the page without a full page load. It also requires clientRender() in the client entrypoint. Turn it off when a page depends on a full document load, for example a page that must run a third-party script on every navigation.
en.goto_desc: goTo from @carats/csr navigates the same way an intercepted link click does. It is the right way to submit a search box or any other form that should not reload the document.
en.routing_suspense_desc: The suspense map supplies the components used when a route cannot produce a page: notFound for an unmatched URL and error for a component or culet that threw. Both are optional, and error receives the thrown Error as its only argument.
en.data_fetching_intro: Server props are the only data channel Carats provides. A culet fetches on the server, and a burnished component receives the result.
en.culet_lifecycle_desc: The server resolves the culet for the requested route before the page component runs, so the component always renders with complete data and there is no loading state to handle. When a culet throws, the error is passed to the error suspense component.
en.culet_args_desc: A culet handler receives everything the request carried: params for the route parameters, plus url, query, headers, cookies and method. There is no data property, because culets are only ever reached by a GET.
en.async_desc: A culet can be async, and awaiting inside it is the normal way to talk to a database or a remote API. Returning a promise is enough; there is no need to await it at the call site.
en.caching_desc: The framework keeps the most recent server props for a route and reuses them, so a burnished component does not refetch on every render. When a page must always show fresh data, opt out per component with the recast option.
en.recast_desc: Wrap the component with { recast: true } to bypass the cache on every render. It applies to that component only, which makes it a good fit for pages such as a live dashboard rather than a whole-site default.
en.ssp_global_desc: The serialized props are exposed on window.carats.ssp. ssp.for is the route they belong to and ssp.data is the value. This is what lets a non-burnished component, or plain code in an afterMount callback, read data that the server already fetched, instead of issuing a second request.
en.culet_matching_desc: A culet is bound to its page purely by route string. The route of the culet and the route of the facet must be character-for-character identical, including parameter names, otherwise the component renders without data. A route with no culet simply renders with no props, which is the normal case for static pages.
en.testing_intro: Components and culets are plain functions, so both can be tested directly. No DOM environment and no rendering library is required.
en.testing_desc: The test script runs Vitest with V8 coverage. Exclude the entrypoints, the facets file and the DTO folder from coverage, since they are wiring rather than logic.
en.testing_component_desc: Call init once from jjsx to install the transpiler, then call transpile with a JSX element to get the HTML string. Asserting on substrings of that string is usually enough and keeps the test free of a DOM.
en.testing_burnish_desc: A burnished component accepts its server props as ordinary props, so the same element renders with mock data in a test exactly as it would on the server.
en.testing_culet_desc: A culet is a function from a request to a value. Pass a plain object with params and call it. There is no server to start, which is the main reason culets are cheap to test.
en.static_generation_intro: The @carats/ssg package prerenders a Carats application to static HTML, which is useful for sites that do not need a live server.
en.static_generation_desc: Add the static build script to package.json. It runs the carats-ssg binary with NODE_ENV=production, so the same build pipeline produces the static output.
en.static_generation_note1: Content that is the same for every visitor, such as marketing pages and documentation.
en.static_generation_note2: Deployments that only need a CDN or a file host.
en.static_generation_note3: Sites that still need per-request data should use the Express integration instead, because a culet may depend on the request.
en.static_generation_cli_note: The carats-ssg binary ships no TypeScript declarations of its own; treat it as a command-line tool and keep the framework types in @carats/ssr.
en.api_reference_intro: Every @carats/* package is small and fully typed. The declarations below are the complete public surface.
en.conventions_intro: Carats resolves a handful of paths and filenames by convention. Deviating from them works until it does not, so it is worth keeping to them.
en.conv_pages_desc: Each route lives in its own folder under src/client/pages, and the folder exports a default component from index.tsx next to a stylesheet of the same name. Folders that start with an underscore are not routes; they are shared building blocks referenced by the routes that need them.
en.conv_layout_desc: There is no file-convention layout like Next.js. A _layout component is imported by the pages that need it, which makes the composition explicit and lets a page opt out. The reference template wraps every page in the same layout to share the header, the footer and the mobile menu.
en.conv_error_desc: The error and notFound suspense components are ordinary components. The error one receives the thrown Error, so it can read message and stack; the notFound one receives nothing. Both are worth wrapping in the shared layout so a failure still renders the site chrome.
en.conv_dto_desc: Interfaces placed in src/dto are global, because typeRoots points at that folder. That is what lets a culet be written as culet<User> with no import in both the server entrypoint and the page component. Keep these files free of imports and runtime code; they are declarations only.
en.conv_sass_desc: A page or component imports its own SASS file, and that file imports base.sass with @use ... as *. The extension is optional in the path. Keep global resets and tokens in base.sass and nothing else there.
en.conv_naming_desc: Route folders are named after the route segment, and the dynamic parameter name must be identical in the facet and in the culet. Culet files are named after the action they perform and default export the culet, which is then seated in the server entrypoint.
en.react_migration_intro: Carats is deliberately close to React, so most component code ports directly. The differences below are the ones that actually break a port.
en.rm_row_runtime_react: React, React DOM and a virtual DOM
en.rm_row_runtime_carats: JJSX only; components are functions returning HTML
en.rm_row_state_carats: use stores a value; the DOM is updated manually
en.rm_row_effect_carats: afterMount (after load) or beforeMount (immediate), no deps
en.rm_row_routing_react: A file-system router with layouts and nested routes
en.rm_row_routing_carats: A defineFacets map, composed by importing a layout
en.rm_row_data_carats: A culet per route plus a Burnish wrapper
en.rm_row_head_react: next/head or the framework metadata export
en.rm_row_meta_carats: defaultProps on the component; no context or memo
en.rm_row_styling_carats: Scoped SASS importing shared design tokens
en.rm_step1: Delete react, react-dom and every React-only dependency.
en.rm_step2: Replace event attributes with addEventListener inside an afterMount or beforeMount callback.
en.rm_step3: Convert every file-based route into an entry in the facets map, and import a shared layout explicitly.
en.rm_step4: Move getServerSideProps bodies into culets, and wrap the page with Burnish.
en.rm_step5: Move useState to use, and add the manual DOM update that the re-render used to do.
en.rm_step6: Move the head export to this.head on a function component.
en.rm_step7: Replace CSS-in-JS with SASS files imported by each component.
en.subscribe_owns_dom_note: Keep the two concerns apart. A handler changes state and a subscriber writes the DOM. A handler that also writes the DOM gives the element two sources of truth, and the moment one of them is missed the page disagrees with itself.
